meta.title: Czech A2
meta.subtitle: 1,161 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Czech → English (see the Czech, recall the meaning) and English → Czech (see an English meaning, recall the Czech). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1,161 words and expressions for level A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM: 1,161 of them are the A2 entries of the official word list of the Czech language exam for permanent residence — the Soupis lexikálních jednotek published by the National Pedagogical Institute of the Czech Republic (NPI ČR) with its reference description of Czech for levels A1 and A2 — that an English dictionary can teach. The list's grammatical patterns ("čekat na", "chtít + infinitive") and the phrases written with a blank or a choice of endings are not cards. One of them is a verb the list names only inside a collocation (povídat si o), taught on its own. No word taught in the levels below is repeated. The cards are ordered by how often each word is met in that frequency list, each word counted over all its forms, so the commonest come first; the 14 multi-word expressions, which a list of single words cannot count, come last. Czech changes the endings of its nouns, adjectives and verbs, and stems change with them, so each card carries the forms that cannot be guessed, read from a dictionary rather than generated. 566 nouns show their gender, three cases of the singular and two of the plural. 247 verbs show their aspect and its partner, the forms for já (I), on (he) and oni (they) and the past of on — a perfective verb's present forms being its future. 21 adjectives show their comparative and superlative. A reflexive verb is taught as the list writes it, with its se or si (bát se, dát si); where the dictionary's meaning says only that a sense is reflexive, it is marked (se/si). Real example sentences come with 926 of the 1,161 entries, three apiece for 728, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Word list: NPI ČR, Soupis lexikálních jednotek A1, A2 (cestina-pro-cizince.cz) — the words only. Meanings, forms and parts of speech: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency ordering: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
